extracted.intended_audience: readers of 18th-century periodicals / scholars of Steele & Addison / general literary-historical readers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting evaluative standards, prescriptive comments, and quality criteria embedded in Steele/Addison Tatler essays (early 18th-century periodical prose) for use in annotation, editing, or criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness over pedantic speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is observed too often, that men of wit do so much employ their thoughts upon fine speculations, that things useful to mankind are wholly neglected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer employing intellectual talent on works of general use rather than abstruse emendations (example given: making emendations upon some enclitics in a Greek author vs correcting obvious, useful matters). Steele recommends remarking such things and recommending their correction to higher powers; anti-pattern is devoting attention to minutiae at expense of public benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in the orthography of public inscriptions and sign-posts
rubrics_metrics.description: There should not be so many gross errors as there are in the very directions of things, wherein accuracy is necessary for the conduct of life (notably inscriptions on sign-posts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mistakes in spelling on signs mislead strangers (anecdote: 'This is the BEER' vs 'This is the BEAR') and are easily amended; actors/painters often render signs unhelpful. Recommendation: maintain and repair public signs' grammar and spelling; anti-pattern is neglect leading to practical inconvenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of place distinction and true characters for public markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Places are confounded, as well for want of proper distinctions, as things for want of true characters (example: mistaking one equestrian statue for another).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public markers (statues, inscriptions) should have distinct, true identifying features to prevent misdirection; failure produces real-world mischief (lost people, wrong lodgings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical proposal for maintaining sign orthography
rubrics_metrics.description: I propose that every tradesman in the cities of London and Westminster shall give me sixpence a quarter for keeping their signs in repair, as to the grammatical part; and I will take into my house a Swiss Count... for despatch sake, setting up the head of the said foreigner for my sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative/financial mechanism suggested to ensure signs are kept grammatically correct (levy a small fee, appoint a memorizer/inspector). Presented as constructive remedy—anti-pattern is leaving correction to chance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value and deservingness of news-writers (journalists) as public servants
rubrics_metrics.description: The ingenious fraternity of news-writers... have been upon parties and skirmishes, made us masters of several strong towns many weeks before our generals could do it... Their case is harder than that of the soldiers; it is impossible for this ingenious sort of men to subsist after a peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News-writers provide vital public service, often inventing or amplifying news in hard times; Steele argues they merit institutional support (proposal: an appendix of apartments at Chelsea Hospital, furnished for decayed news-writers to compile annals). Anti-pattern: neglecting and leaving them destitute after wartime demand ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military leadership should 'husband' a war (economy and sustainability in command)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Duke of Marlborough... has plainly shown himself unacquainted with the arts of husbanding a war. He might have grown as old as the Duke of Alva... and yet have got reputation enough every year for any reasonable man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for good generalship: manage resources and campaign tempo to sustain reputation and avoid unnecessary haste or waste of manpower; anti-pattern: rapid overcommitment leading to later reproach or logistical strain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acting (proper action) can redeem weak drama/dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: This performance is the greatest instance that we can have of the irresistible force of proper action. The dialogue in itself has something too low to bear a criticism upon it: but Mr. Wilks enters into the part with so much skill, that the gallantry, the youth, and gaiety... is looked upon with as much indulgence on the stage, as in real life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In theatrical evaluation, strong physical performance, gesture, and stage presence can overcome deficiencies in the written text; anti-pattern: relying solely on dialogue without effective stagecraft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications and proper character of an esquire
rubrics_metrics.description: An esquire was originally a trusty companion fit for any offices about his master: as gentle and chaste as a gentleman usher, quick and active as an equerry, smooth and eloquent as a master of the ceremonies. Steele proposes that no man shall be received as an esquire who cannot bring a certificate that he has conquered some lady's obdurate heart; that he can lead up a country dance, or carry a message between her and her lover, with address, secrecy and diligence. A squire's credentials shall be signed by three toasts, and one prude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for claiming the title 'Esquire' combine civic/martial service and social/courtly accomplishments; Steele satirically prescribes documentary proof and social endorsements as gatekeeping. Anti-pattern: indiscriminate assumption of the title by clerks, transcribing hands, and rural boors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Female playwrights' talent for subtle plotting in matters of love
rubrics_metrics.description: The plot and incidents of the play are laid with that subtlety of spirit which is peculiar to females of wit, and is very seldom well performed by those of the other sex, in whom craft in love is an act of invention, and not, as with women, the effect of nature and instinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating comedies of intrigue or love plots, credit is given to a natural, subtle handling of amorous craft—stereotypically ascribed here to women writers. Anti-pattern: male writers treating craft in love as artificial invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal/petition practice: plain, explicit allegations and evidence required
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspicions, or guesses at what you mean, nay certainty of it, except you plainly speak it, are no foundation for a formal suit... The affliction you complain of, is to be redressed by law; but... consider what mortifications you are to go through in bringing it into open court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For legal remedies (example: petition for divorce), a client must present explicit, candid statements and supporting facts; mere suspicion or private feeling is insufficient. Also warns of social cost of public suits as part of counseling clients (anti-pattern: vague accusations or seeking legal redress for matters unsupported by clear evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatre organisation and civic usefulness: actors as tradesmen / communal support model
rubrics_metrics.description: In Amsterdam the actors are all of them tradesmen, who, after their day's work is over, earn about a guilder a night by personating kings and generals... The profits of the theatre maintain a hospital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model for theatrical institutions: allow performers to combine trade and art, and dedicate theatrical profits to civic ends (hospitals for decayed wits). Anti-pattern: theatre treated as sole means to private enrichment rather than public philanthropy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diplomatic negotiation style: plainness and exploiting rivals' jealousies
rubrics_metrics.description: Let me beg you therefore, in this representation of our circumstances, to lay aside art, which ceases to be such when it is seen, and make use of all your skill, to gain us what advantages you can from the enemy's jealousy of each other's greatness; which is the place where only you have room for any dexterity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive advice (in a fictional 'letter'): be plain about necessities in negotiation, avoid detectable artifice, and use rivals' mutual jealousies to secure advantages. Anti-pattern: using obvious artifices that when seen destroy persuasion.
